title: Finite multiple harmonic sums and lower-truncated p-adic multiple zeta-star values

definitions.name: x2611_16923_li
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_16923_li (r : ℕ) (weak : Bool) (lower : ℕ)
    (upper : Option ℕ) (L : List (ℕ × (Fin r →₀ ℕ))) : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) ℚ :=
  fun e =>
    ∑ n : Fin L.length → Fin (e.sum (fun _ a => a) + 1),
      if (∀ i, lower ≤ (n i).val) ∧
          (List.ofFn (fun i => (n i).val)).Pairwise
            (fun a b => if weak then a ≤ b else a < b) ∧
          (∀ M ∈ upper, ∀ i, (n i).val < M) ∧
          (∑ i : Fin L.length, (n i).val • (L.get i).2) = e then
        ∏ i : Fin L.length, (((n i).val : ℚ) ^ (L.get i).1)⁻¹
      else 0
definitions.notes: Coefficientwise form of Definition 2.3, restricted to monomial arguments in r formal variables; this covers every argument used in the selected claims. L lists (positive weight, monomial exponent vector) pairs. All uses have nonzero monomial arguments. For coefficient e, every summation index is at most the total degree |e| because each argument has positive degree, so the displayed finite coefficient sum is exactly the infinite formal sum. weak=true means weakly increasing, false means strictly increasing; lower is inclusive and upper, when present, is strict. Empty L gives the constant series 1. Positivity of weights and lower≥1 are enforced in statements, not built into this reusable definition.

definitions.name: x2611_16923_entries
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_16923_entries {r : ℕ} (k : Fin r → ℕ) : List (ℕ × (Fin r →₀ ℕ)) :=
  List.ofFn (fun i => (k i, Finsupp.single i 1))
definitions.notes: Attach the independent variable zᵢ to the i-th weight, represented by its unit exponent vector.

definitions.name: x2611_16923_blocks
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_16923_blocks {r : ℕ} (k : Fin r → ℕ)
    (c : Composition r) : List (ℕ × (Fin r →₀ ℕ)) :=
  List.ofFn (fun h : Fin c.length =>
    ((∑ j : Fin (c.blocksFun h), k (c.embedding h j)),
      ∑ j : Fin (c.blocksFun h), Finsupp.single (c.embedding h j) 1))
definitions.notes: For a composition of r, merge each consecutive block as in (2.3): add weights and add monomial exponent vectors, which multiplies the original arguments.

statements.label: Lemma 2.4
statements.name: x2611_16923_lemma2_4
statements.original:
For every nonempty index $\bm{k}=(k_{1},\ldots,k_{r})$ ,

(2.3)

 $\operatorname{Li}^{\star}_{k_{1},\ldots,k_{r}}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{r})=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq q\leq r\\
0=i_{0}<i_{1}<\cdots<i_{q}=r\end{subarray}}\operatorname{Li}_{K_{1},\ldots,K_{q}}(Z_{1},\ldots,Z_{q}),$ 

where

 $K_{h}=\sum_{\nu=i_{h-1}+1}^{i_{h}}k_{\nu},\qquad Z_{h}=\prod_{\nu=i_{h-1}+1}^{i_{h}}z_{\nu}\qquad(1\leq h\leq q).$
statements.lean: (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (k : Fin r → ℕ) (hk : ∀ i, 0 < k i) : x2611_16923_li r true 1 none (x2611_16923_entries k) = ∑ c : Composition r, x2611_16923_li r false 1 none (x2611_16923_blocks k c)
statements.notes: An equality in ℚ[[z₁,…,zᵣ]]. Fin r uses zero-based positions. Composition r is Mathlib’s finite type of decompositions into consecutive nonempty blocks, exactly the choices 0=i₀<…<i_q=r. Each block sums the weights and multiplies the variables, encoded by adding their monomial exponent vectors. The hypotheses retain nonemptiness and positivity of every entry.

fidelity.twin: (r : ℕ) (hr : 0 < r) (k : Fin r → ℕ) (hk : ∀ i, 0 < k i) : x2611_16923_li r true 1 none (x2611_16923_entries k) = ∑ c : Composition r, x2611_16923_li r false 1 none (x2611_16923_blocks k c)

statements.label: Lemma 2.5
statements.name: x2611_16923_lemma2_5
statements.original:
For every $N\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{\geq 1}$ and every index,

(2.4)

 $\operatorname{Li}^{\star,N\leq}_{k_{1},\ldots,k_{r}}(z_{1},\ldots,z_{r})=\sum_{i=0}^{r}(-1)^{i}\operatorname{Li}^{<N}_{k_{i},\ldots,k_{1}}(z_{i},\ldots,z_{1})\operatorname{Li}^{\star}_{k_{i+1},\ldots,k_{r}}(z_{i+1},\ldots,z_{r})$ 

in ${\mathbb{Q}}[[z_{1},\ldots,z_{r}]]$ .
statements.lean: (N r : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (k : Fin r → ℕ) (hk : ∀ i, 0 < k i) : x2611_16923_li r true N none (x2611_16923_entries k) = ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (r + 1), (-1 : MvPowerSeries (Fin r) ℚ) ^ i * x2611_16923_li r false 1 (some N) ((x2611_16923_entries k).take i).reverse * x2611_16923_li r true 1 none ((x2611_16923_entries k).drop i)
statements.notes: The four variants of Definition 2.3 are encoded with a weak/strict flag, an inclusive lower bound, and an optional strict upper bound. Reversing the first i weight/variable pairs implements both printed reversals. Factors stay in the common r-variable power series ring; unused variables have exponent zero. Includes r=0, with every empty-index factor equal to 1.
